7. Conclusion
The magic of quantum computing lies in the fact that it op-
eratesonthewavefunctionitself. Unlikeclassicalmachines,
whichmanipulatedefinitebits,quantumcomputersmanipulate
probabilities, amplitudes, and correlations that exist before
measurement.Aregisterofqubitsdoesnotjustholdnumbers
—itencodesallpossiblestatesatonce,asuperpositionsovast
thatevenasmalldeviceoutstripstherepresentationalpowerof
allatomsinthevisibleuniverse.Interferencethenactsasakind
ofsculptor,cancellingwrongpathwaysandamplifyinglawful
ones, producing results that cannot be reached by classical
computation.
Thisiswhyquantumcomputingseemsincomprehensibleto
mostpeople.Humanintuitionistrainedontheclassicalworld,
whereobjectsarefixed,eventsfollowlinearcausality,andun-
certaintymeansignorance.Inthequantumworld,bycontrast,
uncertainty is structure. Correlations exist without signals
passingbetweenparticles, outcomesaredeterminedonlyin
relationtomeasurement,andcomputationbecomesadance
ofprobabilitiesratherthanamarchofsteps. Whatfeelslike
“magic” is simply the lawful functioning of nature at scales
whereourintuitionisblind.
The misunderstanding of quantum computing comes from
treatingitasmerely“faster”or“smaller”classicalcomputing.
Intruth,itisadifferentsubstrateoflogic: onewhereerror
correction mirrors DNA proofreading, where entanglement
functionslikebiologicalsynchrony,andwhereresiliencede-
pendsonlawfulstabilisationratherthanbruteforce.Collapse
